item.title: What’s So Great About the B-52 Bomber’s Next Engine?
item.description: In the near future, the US Air Force’s B-52 bombers will be equipped with Rolls-Royce F130 turbofan engines, dramatically expanding their range. The post What’s So Great About the B-52 Bomber’s Next Engine? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: What Is “Bingo Fuel,” And Why Do Fighter Pilots Worry About It?
item.description: “Bingo fuel” is the hard limit of fuel that pilots need in order to safely return to base—a limit that can significantly restrict their mission envelope. The post What Is “Bingo Fuel,” And Why Do Fighter Pilots Worry About It? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Six F-16 Fighting Falcons Are Flying South for the Winter (and Staying There)
item.description: The Argentine Air Force has purchased six secondhand F-16 Fighting Falcon fighter jets from Denmark, following regulatory approval from the United States. The post Six F-16 Fighting Falcons Are Flying South for the Winter (and Staying There) appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Astropolitics After Ukraine: How Sanctions Rewired Russia’s Space Economy
item.description: US sanctions on Russia’s space industry triggered a rapid restructuring, focused on domestic production, Chinese cooperation, and new partners across the Global South. Few observers expected Western sanctions to hit Russia’s space sector as hard—or as quickly—as they did in 2022. item.title: Kremlin Furious After NATO Floats ‘Preemptive’ Actions Against Russia
item.description: An Italian admiral speculated that military action against Russia could still be considered "defensive" in nature, considering Russian hybrid warfare actions against the West. The post Kremlin Furious After NATO Floats ‘Preemptive’ Actions Against Russia appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Will Russia Ever Close Its Su-57 Deal with India?
item.description: Despite the West’s best efforts, India and Russia have maintained close military cooperation—but it is still unclear if New Delhi will buy the Su-57 Felon fighter jet. The post Will Russia Ever Close Its Su-57 Deal with India? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Russia Is Inching Toward a Jets-for-Bases Deal with Sudan
item.description: Russia is expected to imminently open its first African naval base in Sudan, whose government has sought foreign partners to aid in its ongoing civil war. The post Russia Is Inching Toward a Jets-for-Bases Deal with Sudan appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Russia’s Putin Issues Chilling New Threat Against Europe
item.description: Putin is trying to drive a wedge between the United States and Europe and take advantage of any disagreement to further his foreign policy goals in Ukraine. The post Russia’s Putin Issues Chilling New Threat Against Europe appeared first on The National Interest.
